newsitem.title: USA: MLS-DIAZ ARCE SCORES FOUR GOALS AS UNITED ROMP.
newsitem.headline: MLS-DIAZ ARCE SCORES FOUR GOALS AS UNITED ROMP.

text.p: Salvadoran striker Raul Diaz Arce became the first Major League Soccer League player to register a hat trick this season, scoring four goals in D.C. United's 5-2 win over the Colorado Rapids.

Diaz Arce, who finished second in scoring (23 goals) last season, found the back of the net in the ninth, 26th, 64th (penalty kick) and 86th minutes for United (3-0) in a game played Saturday in temperatures well below freezing.
Bolivian Jaime Moreno added a goal for the defending champions in the 76th minute before a crowd of 4,434 at Mile High Stadium, the smallest crowd in league history.
Former U.S. national team captain Peter Vermes and Chris Henderson scored first-half goals for the Rapids (1-2).

Carlos Alberto Parreira, who directed Brazil to the 1994 World Cup championship, recorded his first victory as coach of the New York/New Jersey MetroStars (1-3) in the team's home opener in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Venezuelan international Giovanni Savarese scored in each half in a 3-1 victory over the New England Revolution (1-2) and former Italian World Cup goalkeeper Walter Zenga.
Second-half substitute A.J. Wood added a late insurance goal. Defender Sam George had given New England an early 1-0 lead.

The Tampa Bay Mutiny remained unbeaten in their opening three games as midfielder Steve Ralston, last year's rookie of the year, broke a 1-1 tie in the 81st minute for a 2-1 win over the Kansas City Wizards (2-1) in a matchup of conference leaders in Tampa, Florida.

Colombian National Team midfielder Carlos Valderrama converted a penalty kick in the 36th minute after one-time Scottish international Mo Johnston tripped Giuseppe Galderisi in the penalty area. Preki equalised for Kansas City in the 60th minute.
Eric Wynalda, the U.S. national team's all-time goal-scorer, turned playmaker in the San Jose Clash's 4-1 triumph over the Los Angeles Galaxy in San Jose, California.

Wynalda set up two goals, including the go-ahead goal on a free kick to defender John Doyle in the 61st minute. Dominic Kinnear scored off Wynalda's cross for the first San Jose goal. Ronald Cerritos and Hungarian Istvan Urbanyi, who practiced only once with the Clash after joining the team Friday, also tallied.

Salvadoran Mauricio Cienfuegos scored the Galaxy's lone goal in the 39th minute, the first goal the Clash (2-2) allowed at home in 255 minutes dating back to the final regular-season game. The Galaxy (0-3), which rolled to a 12-0 start last season and reached the championship game, is the only winless team in the 10-team league.

U.S. international Brian McBride's second goal of the match, a penalty kick in the 75th minute, lifted the Columbus Crew (2-1) over the Dallas Burn (1-2) in Columbus, Ohio. Jorge Rodriguez scored for Dallas.
